Alder and Kell lie 30 kilometers inland, to the west and east. A regional climatologist concludes that the lake's downwind shore receives far heavier snowfall than its upwind shore. items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the example?
choices: Easton averaged 60 cm more snow per year than Kell, which also lies east of the lake.
Westport averaged 20 cm more snow per year than Alder, which also lies west of the lake.
Easton averaged three times as much snow per year as Westport, on the opposite shore.
Kell averaged less snow per year than Westport, despite lying east of the lake.
items.explanation: Start with the direction. The wind blows west to east, so the eastern shore is downwind and the western shore is upwind. items.stimulus:
In drypoint, an artist scratches lines straight into a copper plate. This throws up a ridge of metal, the burr, which holds extra ink and prints a soft, velvety line. Each pass through the press flattens the burr a little. Etched lines, bitten into the plate by acid, have no burr to lose. Conservator Ines Valdés argues that drypoint plates therefore wear out far sooner than etched ones. In her printing trial, ______

Line Detail Retained Compared with First Proof (%)
Impression | Drypoint plate | Etched plate
10th | 96 | 99
30th | 71 | 97
50th | 44 | 95
items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
choices: both plates kept more than 90% of their line detail through the 10th impression.
the etched plate kept 99% of its line detail at the 10th impression and 97% at the 30th.
the drypoint plate kept more detail at the 50th impression than the etched plate did at the 30th.
from the 10th to the 50th impression, the drypoint plate lost 52 points of detail and the etched plate 4.
items.explanation: Valdés claims drypoint plates wear out *far sooner* than etched ones. To show that, you need both plates' loss over the same run of impressions. items.stimulus: Endurance athletes lose sodium in sweat, and low blood sodium can hasten fatigue. Because athletes sweat more in heat, this loss is greatest on hot days. A team of sports scientists had cyclists ride to exhaustion in a cool room and in a hot room. The cyclists drank either plain water or an otherwise identical drink with added sodium. The team concluded that the sodium drink lessened, though it did not eliminate, the toll that heat took on endurance: for example, ______
items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the example?
choices: in cool conditions, cyclists rode for 60 minutes whether they drank water or the sodium drink.
with water, cyclists rode for 60 minutes in cool conditions but only 36 minutes in hot conditions.
moving from cool to hot conditions cut riding time by 24 minutes with the sodium drink but by 12 with water.
moving from cool to hot conditions cut riding time by 12 minutes with the sodium drink but by 24 with water.
items.explanation: First work out what the sentence needs: the drop caused by heat should be smaller with the sodium drink than with water, and it still shouldn't be zero. Cooking pots absorb fats from the food prepared in them, and chemical tests on these residues can show whether a household cooked fish. The burr holds ink, but each pass through the press flattens it, so the lines fade from one print to the next. Etched lines are cut deeper by acid and wear more slowly. A thin electroplated layer of steel protects both kinds of line. Printmaker Tobias Wren concluded that steel facing multiplies the life of drypoint lines far more than the life of etched lines. For example, ______

Prints Made Before Visible Line Wear
Line type | Unfaced plate | Steel-faced plate
Drypoint | 20 | 180
Etched | 150 | 300
items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the example?
choices: steel facing added 160 prints to the life of drypoint lines and 150 prints to the life of etched lines.
steel-faced plates with etched lines yielded 300 prints, the most of any plate in the table.
steel facing let drypoint plates yield nine times as many prints, but etched plates only twice as many.
steel facing multiplied the number of prints from etched plates by more than it did for drypoint plates.
items.explanation: Wren's claim is about how many times longer steel facing makes the lines last, so you need ratios, not differences. Drypoint goes from 20 to 180 prints, which is 9 times as many. D.why: This reverses the comparison. Etched plates gain by a factor of 2 and drypoint plates by a factor of 9, so drypoint is multiplied by far more.

Trees in cooler climates tend to have leaves with toothed rather than smooth edges, so paleobotanists often estimate past temperatures from the percentage of toothed-margin species in a fossil flora. Paleobotanist Ines Haldane cautions that the method can mislead. Flora | Setting | Temperature from isotope data (°C) | Toothed-margin species (%)
P | Streamside | 18 | 41
Q | Upland lake | 18 | 27
R | Streamside | 14 | 55
S | Upland lake | 14 | 38
items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the example?
choices: Flora P (streamside, 18°C) had a higher percentage of toothed-margin species than Flora Q (upland lake, 18°C) did.
Flora R (streamside, 14°C) had a higher percentage of toothed-margin species than Flora Q (upland lake, 18°C) did.
Flora S (upland lake, 14°C) had a higher percentage of toothed-margin species than Flora Q (upland lake, 18°C) did.
Flora S (upland lake, 14°C) had a higher percentage of toothed-margin species than Flora R (streamside, 14°C) did.

So the example has to compare a streamside flora with a non-streamside flora at the same temperature, and the streamside flora has to have the higher percentage. Floras P and Q were both 18°C, P is streamside, and P has 41% against Q's 27%. Setting is the only thing that differs between them, so the difference can be put down to setting.

But R is also 4°C cooler than Q, and cooler climates have more toothed species anyway. The gap could come entirely from temperature, so it doesn't show what setting does when temperature is held equal.

items.stimulus: City planners often widen sidewalks by narrowing traffic lanes, expecting the added room to draw more pedestrians. In hot months, however, unshaded concrete absorbs heat, and hot pavement discourages walking, so extra sidewalk space may attract few people unless something keeps it cool. After studying 40 downtown blocks from 2023 to 2025, urban planner Tomás Reyes-Whitfield concluded that widening sidewalks increased summer afternoon foot traffic only on blocks where street trees shaded the sidewalk. For example, ______
items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the graph to complete the example?
choices: widened, shaded blocks gained 24%, versus 8% for unwidened, shaded blocks, while widened and unwidened unshaded blocks each gained 4%.
widened, shaded blocks gained 24%, versus 4% for widened, unshaded blocks, while unwidened, shaded blocks gained just 8%.
widened, shaded blocks gained 24%, versus 4% for unwidened, unshaded blocks, while unwidened, shaded blocks gained just 8%.
widened, shaded blocks gained 24%, versus 8% for unwidened, shaded blocks, while widened, unshaded blocks gained more than unwidened ones.
items.explanation: The word 'only' means the example has to show two things. First, among shaded blocks, widening raised foot traffic: widened blocks gained 24% and unwidened blocks gained 8%. Second, among unshaded blocks, widening made no difference: widened and unwidened blocks both gained 4%. Choice A is the only option that states both comparisons, each with shade held constant. Together they show that widening helped where there was shade and did not help where there wasn't.

B.why: These numbers are read correctly, but the main comparison (24% versus 4%) is between two widened blocks that differ in shade. That shows shade matters once a sidewalk is widened. But it finishes by misreading the graph: widened and unwidened unshaded blocks both gained 4%, so neither gained more. And if widening had helped unshaded blocks, that would undercut the word 'only' in the claim rather than support it.

items.stimulus:
Some self-healing plastics contain tiny capsules of liquid resin that burst when a crack forms and fill the gap. Heat can also close cracks on its own, by letting polymer chains flow. A team that tested otherwise identical samples with and without capsules cautioned that their headline result, 75 percent strength recovery at 60°C, overstates what the capsules themselves achieve, since ______

Strength Recovered After Healing (%)
Healing temperature | With capsules | Without capsules
20°C | 35 | 5
60°C | 75 | 40
items.stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
choices: samples without capsules recovered 40 percent of their strength when healed at 60°C.
samples with capsules recovered 75 percent of their strength at 60°C, the highest figure in the table.
at 60°C, samples with capsules recovered more strength than samples without capsules did.
at 60°C, samples without capsules recovered more strength than samples with capsules did.
items.explanation: To show that 75% overstates what the capsules do, you need the share of that recovery that would happen without them. Capsule-free samples at the same temperature recovered 40% from heat alone, so the capsules account for only about 35 of the 75 points.

B.why: This only restates the headline figure. It gives no baseline to compare it with, so it can't show that the figure overstates anything.

C.why: This is true, but it shows the capsules helping, which is the opposite of the team's warning. You picked a correct reading that points the wrong way.

D.why: This reverses the 60°C row. Samples without capsules recovered 40%, which is less than the 75% recovered by samples with capsules.
